newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Santos to have new FCOJ terminal by Dec.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Santos to have new FCOJ terminal by Dec.

text.p: Brazil's key port of Santos should have another frozen concentrated orange juice (FCOJ) terminal operational by December, according to the CODESP port authority.
The new terminal is being built by Rhamo Comerical and is the eleventh leasing agreement signed between CODESP and a private sector company, the company said in a statement.
According to Rhamo director Rogerio Carvalho Brago, Rhamo is to invest around $11 million in installing storage and operational equipment in the 8,000 square meter area, the CODESP statement said.
Total storage capacity should reach 22,000 tonnes and the terminal is expected to handle around 130,000 tonnes a year.
Existing buildings on the site have already been pulled down and work is beginning on building the cold storage room, a CODESP spokeswoman said.
Exports of FCOJ from CODESP berths reached 527,637 tonnes in 1996, up from 448,602 tonnes in 1995, according to CODESP statistics.
In addition, exports from Cutrale's private terminal at the port totaled 259,300 tonnes last year, slightly up from 228,512 tonnes the previous year.
The new terminal would help in reducing costs but does not mean Brazilian FCOJ exports will rise sharply, analysts said.
"I think the growth in Brazilian juice exports will be around two to three percent a year," one analyst said.
"The margins at the moment are very small. A lot of small companies have closed, others are in trouble. There is a real concentration going on," he added.
